options.text: Juice particles can move and change positions while staying close under attraction, so shape changes but volume stays fixed.
Juice particles are locked in fixed places, so the juice cannot change shape at all.
Juice particles fly far apart and fill every corner, so the volume grows to match the lunch-box section.
The lunch-box section sets a new, smaller volume for the same juice as soon as the shape changes.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Leela measures 120 cm³ of fruit juice in a measuring cylinder, then pours it into a square section of her lunch box. The juice takes the square section's shape, but its volume stays 120 cm³.

part_answers.answer: In a liquid, particles move enough to take the container's shape but stay close enough that the volume stays the same.

teacher.key_rationale: Liquid particles move within a limited space while remaining close under attraction, so liquids take the container's shape but keep a fixed volume.
